newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's total overseas debt falls 3.5 pct in Mch qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ's total overseas debt falls 3.5 pct in Mch qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's total overseas debt fell 3.5 percent in the March quarter to NZ$75.5 billion, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday.
Net repayments, estimated at $2.8 billion accounted for all of the fall.
Exchange rate losses, estimated at less $100 million, were negligible, SNZ said.
New Zealand's overseas debt to GDP ratio at March 31 was 79.4 percent against 84.5 percent at December 31 and 80.4 percent a year ago.
Economists had forecast total debt would be at $79.75 percent.

Official government sector overseas debt fell $1.7 billion in the quarter. This was the third consecutive fall in official sector overseas debt, caused by continued repayments of foreign currency debt.

SNZ said official sector overseas debt denominated in NZ dollars had remained relatively flat over the past three quarters, mainly because foreign holdings of official sector domestically issued securities was relatively unchanged over that period.

Corporate sector overseas debt was down $1.1 billion to $54.8 billion in the quarter. The major influence was a fall in non-resident NZ dollar denominated deposits in New Zealand financial institutions, partly offset by higher overseas issued corporate sector bills and bonds.
The fall in corporate sector overseas debt in the March quarter was only the second fall in that sector in the past 10 quarters.
New Zealand's total overseas debt held as deposits, bills and bonds, and loans fell $1.5 billion, $800 million and $500 million respectively in the quarter.
Non-resident deposits in NZ financial institutions fell for the second quarter, following a variable but general rise over the past three years.
Overseas issued bills and bonds have been in general decline over the past three years, while overseas loans have generally been rising over the past nine quarters.
